1.explanation: All of these files participate in the Tabs implementation and will need updates to support a new “secondary” variant. In packages/react/.../Tabs we must update the React wrapper (Tabs.js) to accept a new prop (e.g. “type” or “variant”) and apply the correct CSS modifier class, update the index.js so that prop flows downstream, add a Storybook example in Tabs-story.js, and add or relax the test in Tabs-test.js. In the core web-component layer (packages/components/src/components/tabs), tabs.config.js controls which props are allowed on the element and tabs.js contains the DOM templating and CSS class logic; both must be extended to recognize and render the new secondary modifier class so that the style can be consumed by React and any other framework.
1.bug_scenario: The Tabs component in carbon-components-react only has a single “primary” style by default. In our design we need to offer a “secondary” variant (see screenshot) where the active tab is underlined in the base text color and the inactive tabs use a light gray text and border. The ask is to bake that new look directly into the Carbon Tabs API (instead of a one-off CSS file) so users can choose “secondary” styling via a prop. The image shows two tabs (“Application Discovery” and “Enterprise Artifacts”) rendered side-by-side in the new secondary style.

2.explanation:
1. packages/components/src/components/tabs/tabs.config.js: This file drives the SCSS/token generation for the Tabs component. To introduce a secondary style, you’ll need to add new token mappings or modifier class names here so the CSS output includes the alternative look.  
2. packages/components/src/components/tabs/tabs.js: The core Web Component wrapper that assigns CSS class names. It needs to recognize a new variant prop (e.g. `kind="secondary"`) and apply a modifier class (e.g. `bx--tabs--secondary`).  
3. packages/react/src/components/Tabs/Tabs.js: The React wrapper currently hard‐codes the base class. You must expand its propTypes and defaultProps to accept the variant prop and forward the correct CSS class to the underlying component.  
4. packages/react/src/components/Tabs/Tabs-story.js: The Storybook story needs to demonstrate the new secondary variant so designers and consumers can preview it.  
5. packages/react/src/components/Tabs/Tabs-test.js: Unit tests for the React Tabs must be updated to assert that the correct modifier class is rendered when the secondary variant is passed, ensuring the change is covered by CI.
2.bug_scenario: The issue is a request for a new “secondary” styling variant for the Tabs component in Carbon. In the screenshot, the active tab (“Application Discovery”) is rendered with a blue highlight and bold text, while the inactive tab (“Enterprise Artifacts”) appears with a lighter background and grey text. Out of the box, Carbon only provides one tabs style, so we need to extend both the core component styling and the React wrapper to accept and render a second, alternative style (e.g. via a new “kind” or “variant” prop).
